cards.explanation: The answer is the glory of the LORD, friends. The prophet Isaiah says darkness covers the earth, "but the LORD will rise upon you, and His glory will appear over you." (Isaiah 60:2) Thick darkness over the peoples, and the LORD's glory over Zion. One little word, "but," and the whole mood flips.

The answer is False. Isaiah says the nations don't stay away: "Nations will come to your light, and kings to the brightness of your dawn." (Isaiah 60:3) So the world is dark, and nations and even kings are coming to Zion's light. I'd show up for that too, friends.

The answer is Zion's own sons and daughters. Isaiah says, "your sons will come from afar, and your daughters will be carried on the arm." (Isaiah 60:4) Sons coming from afar, daughters carried on the arm. Now that's a picture, friends.

The answer is the sea. Isaiah says Zion will be radiant and her heart will swell with joy, "…because the riches of the sea will be brought to you…" (Isaiah 60:5) And the wealth of the nations comes right along with it. That's a lot of arrivals for one city, bakers.

The answer is gold and frankincense, friends. Isaiah says, "…all from Sheba will come, bearing gold and frankincense and proclaiming the praises of the LORD." (Isaiah 60:6) Gold and frankincense, plus praise on the way in. I'd call that a gift with a soundtrack.

The answer is True. Isaiah says they come "…bearing gold and frankincense and proclaiming the praises of the LORD." (Isaiah 60:6) So they arrive with gifts and with praise. That's a whole lot of arriving, friends.

The answer is altar. The LORD says the rams of Nebaioth "…will serve you and go up on My altar with acceptance…" (Isaiah 60:7) Then He says He will adorn His glorious house. Nebaioth's rams are headed there, friends.

The answer is the ships of Tarshish. The LORD says, "Surely the islands will wait for Me, with the ships of Tarshish in the lead, to bring your children from afar…" (Isaiah 60:9) They're in the lead. Front of the line, friends.

The answer is False, they bring plenty. The LORD says the ships will bring Zion's children from afar "…with their silver and gold, to the honor of the LORD your God, the Holy One of Israel, for He has glorified you." (Isaiah 60:9) Silver and gold ride along with them, bakers.

The answer is mercy. The LORD says, "Although I struck you in anger, yet in favor I will show you mercy." (Isaiah 60:10) That's a verse worth reading twice, friends. The anger was real, and so is the favor and mercy that follows.

The answer is never, day or night. The LORD says, "Your gates will always stand open; they will never be shut, day or night…" (Isaiah 60:11) Open all day, open all night, and no sign hanging on the door. I'd leave my oven door open too, but that's a bad idea, friends.

The answer is True, and I think this one is heavy. The LORD says, "For the nation or kingdom that will not serve you will perish; it will be utterly destroyed." (Isaiah 60:12) It's a sober verse in a chapter full of light, and I'll just let it stand as written.

The answer is sanctuary. The LORD says Lebanon's cypress, elm and boxwood will come "…to adorn the place of My sanctuary, and I will glorify the place of My feet." (Isaiah 60:13) The trees are for His holy place. And the LORD Himself says He will glorify it, friends.

The answer is False. Isaiah says, "The sons of your oppressors will come and bow down to you; all who reviled you will fall facedown at your feet…" (Isaiah 60:14) The sons of her oppressors come to bow down. And those who reviled her fall facedown at her feet, friends.

The answer is the City of the LORD, friends. They will "…call you the City of the LORD, Zion of the Holy One of Israel." (Isaiah 60:14) The people who once reviled Zion are the ones saying it. That's quite a turn.

The answer is joy! The LORD says, "…I will make you an everlasting pride, a joy from age to age." (Isaiah 60:15) Forsaken and despised before, and now joy from age to age. That's a big change, friends.

The answer is True. The LORD says, "you will know that I, the LORD, am your Savior and your Redeemer, the Mighty One of Jacob." (Isaiah 60:16) Savior, Redeemer, Mighty One. Zion will know who He is, friends.

The answer is silver! The LORD says, "Instead of bronze I will bring you gold; I will bring silver in place of iron, bronze instead of wood, and iron instead of stones." (Isaiah 60:17) Every swap in that list is a step up. I may need a swap like that for my own chef's hat, bakers.

The answer is True. The LORD says, "I will appoint peace as your governor and righteousness as your ruler." (Isaiah 60:17) Peace governing and righteousness ruling. That sounds like a great place to live, friends.

The answer is Salvation! The LORD says, "But you will name your walls Salvation and your gates Praise." (Isaiah 60:18) Walls named Salvation and gates named Praise. Now that's a sign worth hanging up, friends.

The answer is the LORD Himself. Isaiah says, "…the LORD will be your everlasting light, and your God will be your splendor." (Isaiah 60:19) The sun and moon are no longer her light, and the LORD is, friends.

The answer is True. Isaiah says, "…the LORD will be your everlasting light, and the days of your sorrow will cease." (Isaiah 60:20) Everlasting light, and sorrow comes to an end. That's a good line to hold onto, friends.

The answer is so that He may be glorified. Zion's people are "…the branch of My planting, the work of My hands, so that I may be glorified." (Isaiah 60:21) The reason the LORD gives is His own glory. Planted and made by Him, for Him, friends.

The answer is in its time and quickly. The LORD says, "I am the LORD; in its time I will accomplish it quickly." (Isaiah 60:22) The timing is in His hands, and when the time comes, He moves fast. That's a chapter finished, bakers.
